author: HunterADH
content: Yeah I think that would be an interesting test. I think from a high level vision for the project, you would say that everything is on chain, asset ownership, game logic, etc... But Solana is evolving, and it makes sense to not sacrifice a usable product to be "true" to the vision. If small players can't play because transactions kill the game, then it's probably a better decision to minimize. At least until you have faith Solana can keep tx fees under control.

author: [SAI] Sim [STAR]
content: I thought quite a lot about cargo and how that could mitigate fees. I think all pretty much end with that, with cargo being too small and this increasing the overhead. I think we could play with item sizes instead of ship cargo capacities and fine-tune those. At the end of the day, they both lead to the same result. This could help mitigate more the issue with basic resources, so it could affect small players less. For example, we could halve hydrogen size so that small players farming hydrogen in CSS would benefit from it. This would be the min/max tradeoff, I suppose. Rebalancing every ship's cargo capacity would be too disruptive unless you apply a flat multiplier to all current ships overall.

author: [AEP] Boen
content: Here's the math.  Let's say a normal day is 15B LP.  Then the installed atlas value per FS is: 0.0389  Let's say all the FS gets installed in one day, and the LP shoots up to 35B (which is what it should be).  The value per FS is: 0.0167. content:
The question is whether the 4 amigos will take a drop from 
68% profit -> to 24.4% profit to snipe the first day or if they spread it out over multiple days to maintain max profit.   If they spread it out over multiple days then everyone else gets to participate and that's the main goal.

No one else can compete because you need 100k crew and 30+ sledgbarges.  This is not to be confused with "depositing shortly before epoch end" which is a non-issue.

This is disproportionate inequality because it means only the ultra rich can (top 3 players) can participate in this loop.

With auto redemption players will no longer be incentived to snipe in 8 hours so other players will have a chance to participate.  It's a win for everyone.

author: [AEP] Funcracker [AEP]
content:
I asked myself why SA don't have mass adoption yet, and i realized that only few people is interested in managerial/strategic games like sage; mass adoption people likes games like GTA and fortnite, they want to fire, race, etc; definitively they like more simple games; so i think that the team have to focus first in developing UE5 part of the game; to be clear, i don't like firing and racing, so i will continue playing sage, but if we want mass adoption we have to think to other people too; thera are no games like SA, but if we don't want to lose our competitive advantege we have to go toward mass adoption as soon as possible 

@diegomtx I'm not sure I agree with your statements tbh.
There is no mass adoption yet for a number of reasons. To name a few:
We're not even at 10% of the gameplay, everything is pre-Alpha/Labs level,No marketing,No great profits (for a median investment - see yesterday's Brew),
I am quite sure that indeed the group of gamers interested in managerial/strategic games is dwarfed by the amount of people who like GTA/Fortnite (shooting, racing, etc). I personally feel that it's pretty awesome we'll eventually get most of that gameplay as well, but the spotlight has always been on the Grand Strategy/MMO side of things. We're clearly not anywhere close to having a strategy MMO game  that can stand on its own, but (I feel) the team is doing a solid job experimenting & iterating to get us there.

Regarding focus, the team is focusing most manpower on UE5. But the few people working on SAGE are contrbuting to UE5 as well, as the on-chain aspects will be integratEd into UE5 one day, to add the Grand Strategy gameplay into the main game.

I think it's great that the team focused on the third person shooter mode (and racing, but fans of racing are also outnumbered by shooter-fans, I believe) for a bit, and I'm pretty sure we'll soon hear that the team will double down on that some more. Though it was never a spotlight feature, more low hanging fruit some team members picked up, I do feel this will give us some cool, high-octane, button-mashing gameplay, side-by-side to the slower economic gameplay of SAGE.

All in all, I don't feel there is a competitive advantage to lose at this time, as we are still working towards creating one. I also don't think the team should pivot to focus on the sort of gameplay that could lead to mass-adoption, as this would alienate the existing community and they would just become another Web3 shooter (for example) of which there are many (in development).

In the end we are in year 3 of a 8+ year development cycle. That is something to keep in mind throughout our experience here, I feel.

Anyway, just some thoughts

author: Kr1gs
content:
2023 Chris: "IDK why anyone would want to multi-faction" 
2024 Chris: "We expected people to maximize multi-faction and faction hop, its designed that way" 
Also team - we want to incentivize single faction/single account

To Chris's point (I know he's not reading this), "LP mechanics have been in the roadmap for a while now, no one brought up anything against it".  It WAS brought up, the question of "What prevents a player from just switching to the lowest earning LP faction to claim those rewards?" went unanswered.  Yesterday, Chris referred to this now as "strategic deployment of capital" which is interesting because in the past Chris has not seen the value of multi-factioning. 

Swags has acknowledged that the LP balancing mechanism, while achieving the desired effect, has undesired outcomes...i.e. it was believed that new players would join the lowest faction but instead we find the original question of faction hopping to be true.

Not saying what right or wrong, just providing historical context of team comments and statements.  Yes I keep records 

My assessment is that there's even internal debate on the matter that we don't see and that the team's stance on it has shifted over the years.

author: diegomtxUstur
content: > I asked myself why SA don't have mass adoption yet, and i realized that only few people is interested in managerial/strategic games like sage; mass adoption people likes games like GTA and fortnite, they want to fire, race, etc; definitively they like more simple games; so i think that the team have to focus first in developing UE5 part of the game; to be clear, i don't like firing and racing, so i will continue playing sage, but if we want mass adoption we have to think to other people too; thera are no games like SA, but if we don't want to lose our competitive advantege we have to go toward mass adoption as soon as possible   @diegomtx I'm not sure I agree with your statements tbh. There is no mass adoption yet for a number of reasons. To name a few: We're not even at 10% of the gameplay, everything is pre-Alpha/Labs level,No marketing,No great profits (for a median investment - see yesterday's Brew), I am quite sure that indeed the group of gamers interested in managerial/strategic games is dwarfed by the amount of people who like GTA/Fortnite (shooting, racing, etc). I personally feel that it's pretty awesome we'll eventually get most of that gameplay as well, but the spotlight has always been on the Grand Strategy/MMO side of things. We're clearly not anywhere close to having a strategy MMO game  that can stand on its own, but (I feel) the team is doing a solid job experimenting & iterating to get us there.  Regarding focus, the team is focusing most manpower on UE5. But the few people working on SAGE are contrbuting to UE5 as well, as the on-chain aspects will be integratEd into UE5 one day, to add the Grand Strategy gameplay into the main game.  I think it's great that the team focused on the third person shooter mode (and racing, but fans of racing are also outnumbered by shooter-fans, I believe) for a bit, and I'm pretty sure we'll soon hear that the team will double down on that some more. Though it was never a spotlight feature, more low hanging fruit some team members picked up, I do feel this will give us some cool, high-octane, button-mashing gameplay, side-by-side to the slower economic gameplay of SAGE.  All in all, I don't feel there is a competitive advantage to lose at this time, as we are still working towards creating one. I also don't think the team should pivot to focus on the sort of gameplay that could lead to mass-adoption, as this would alienate the existing community and they would just become another Web3 shooter (for example) of which there are many (in development).  In the end we are in year 3 of a 8+ year development cycle. That is something to keep in mind throughout our experience here, I feel.  Anyway, just some thoughts

author: [AEP] Boen
content: Yup. When a player can instantly warp between factions: 8 Tree Arrows, 6 C11s, 14 Sledbarges, 4 IMPs, 2 JODs, 2 Guardians, 2 Bomaberellas, 9 TAPs,  32 TIPS, 9 OMs, 3 C9s, 1 ARC, 1 R9,  and 35,000 Crew, it raises a lot of questions about disproportionate inequality.   Because this player can close this game loop out before anyone else can, no one else has access to it.  Naturally the Sage Game manual has multiple checks against this type of gameplay but none of them have made it to the current version.   While smaller players are at 0% revenue due to fees, the top 10 wallets (8 players) are hoovering up over 45% of LP revenue.  This number is growing and with the addition of radiation absorbers from T3 upgrades AND the power of compounding,  his number will likely climb to 60%.   I'm not sure if the top 10 wallets (8 players) hoovering up 60% of the games is good or bad because its a complex economic question but it doesn't seem good to me.  I'm also expecting the top 3 players LP revenue to increase from 28.32% to at least 40% over the next month.  LP opportunities are getting more scarce because Starbases are filling up.  This puts further emphasis on sniping Starbase upgrades.  And since the top 3 players will be hammering Radiation Absorbers which have 1.6x the LP of field stabilizers, this is not a far reach.  These numbers are based on Swagners lastest estimation of 2+ weeks before Auto-redemption is kicked on.  While auto-redemption is not the answer to everything, it will prevent the 8 hour Starbase sniping so all players can participate in Field Stabs and Radiation absorber upgrades.  If auto redemption can give even a 36 hour breather it will be a huge win for everyone involved.

author: [Λ] Sawyn [BR] [STAR]
content:
@SW4GN3R Hello, after a long time observing Based, I see that a mechanic that helped small players a lot, SDU, has lost its luster. I believe this is directly related to the way it is used within the game.

From what I understand, the SDU is an item that represents knowledge (a map, a guide or even an instruction manual). but nothing else in the game uses this knowledge. Even with the growth of SB, we can see that the SDU is the discarded item, filled last just because it has to be. Ships currently launched do not use it.

So I wanted to know your opinion regarding a possible change in the need for this item.

In conjunction with the “instant LP” mechanic suggested in the last Brew, I believe a change to the way SDUs are installed would make them at least a commodity.

This mechanic aims to make knowledge a requirement for installing an item. I'm not talking about a 1x1 scale.

Let's look at an example of hypothetical numbers.
let's say that to go from SB T0 to T1 you need 10M of Framework, 10M of electronics and 400 SDU's.
Instead of leaving the SDU as a separate installation, define that: for someone to install 10M of Framework they will have to install 150 SDU at the same time, (which would mean reading the manual to install the Framework correctly). Now, if someone is going to install the Electronics 10M, they will need to have it in their possession and install the 250SDU together.


This would make the SDU once again relevant at the point of knowledge, the small one that cannot compete with the large mining companies would create an item that is useful, as the large one will need this knowledge to carry out the final operational actions and would also have to transform the SDU from a separate item into a defined item.

Instead of leaving the SDU as a separate installation, define that: for someone to install 10M of Framework they will have to install 150 SDU at the same time, (which would mean reading the manual to install the Framework correctly). Now, if someone is going to install the Electronics 10M, they will need to have it in their possession and install the 250SDU together. This would make the SDU once again relevant at the point of knowledge, the small one that cannot compete with the large mining companies would create an item that is useful, as the large one will need this knowledge to carry out the final operational actions and would also have to transform the SDU from a separate item into a defined item.

author: [SAI] Sim [STAR]
content:
Personally, I believe that one of the biggest obstacles for new players, along with not-so-appealing graphics and a lack of intuitiveness (which, on the other hand, characterizes many management games, at least those from a few years ago), is the high economic threshold. I don't want to reiterate the point that SA is not just a game but a metaverse, etc., etc., but the reality is that fun shouldn't depend on how much one invests in a game; otherwise, it wouldn't be very different from a typical Pay-to-Win. The fact is that even investing a modest but not insignificant amount for a regular player, like $80 (the cost of a triple-A game), doesn't actually lead to any fun because the possibilities would be very, very limited, realistically speaking. 

It would already be different if one could start working on their "base" now, like a Claim Stake, a sort of Farmville where one could perceive their game progress, or even on the construction of the much-anticipated modules and components to make ships customizable (at least technically), thus providing a sense of progression in the game.

What scares me a bit is that I can't get an idea of the timelines. Beyond FC, which will be released at the end of the year, is there a chance to have these radical changes before FC and to also gamify Starbased?

I agree, but that's not going to happen in SAGE any time soon.

In the next year, we're going to see a clear segmentation of the user base into:

SAGE players,More traditional gamers playing UE5 game modes,
SAGE is really phase 1 of the economy.  It's built for hardcore gaming nerds and WEB3 crypto enthusiasts.  It's a true capitalistic design and it's not really built for smaller players on small budgets.
Yes, there's upgrades they can make but it's not going to "save" the smaller players.

Smaller players will be able to enter UE5 game modes with $10-$15 and a few bucks of R4 and have fun.

A small sliver of the UE5 players will want to go deeper and they'll invest in ships to play SAGE.

A few years in the future, all of these game modes will fuse together into the ultimate vision.

author: Buzzec
content: NFTs are individualized. If we were to do normal NFTs for crew we'd be looking at $100m+ of rent, cNFTs allow for data compression by storing the data off-chain/on the ledger with a verification of the data on-chain. Ships right now are SFTs. SFTs allow for multiple tokens to share the smae meta data which saves massively on rent cost at the trade-off that each token is not individualized. Every ship token is equal to all other same type ship tokens

reply.preview: Original message was deleted

author: Buzzec
content: Eventually these will be converted to individualized tokens, need to resolve the rent cost issue as well

author: Buzzec
content: cNFTs are also hard to work with due to the verification mechanism inherit to the data compression

author: Buzzec
content: cNFTs and NFTs also are difficult to transfer en-masse since they are individual tokens. You can easily transfer 10,000 airbikes since it doesn't matter which 10,000 you transfer but with crew you have to tell the chain which 10,000. We're working on this issue now

content: May or may not be, don't want to saddle our users with a massive rent bill

author: DominicVainMod
content: The meta of faction hop / lp snipe / drip was solved with the auto redemption / redemption depreciation. I’ll note that None of the players implementing this tactic spoke out against that solution since it was a good update that solved the issue. To the point, This chart compares the lp per component relative to the time it takes to craft and deposit the final value is the “adjusted” column (bigger number = better) *LP / (craft time + deposit time). It doesn’t take into account transport nor mining but those metrics are mostly irrelevant since crew is by far the largest bottleneck.   Before the lp update these numbers scaled (although too aggressively) while emags, power source, and electronics were relatively similar. One thing that I’ll note that’s positive with the update is FS is the highest but that’s reasonable since it’s the only component that wasn’t stockpiled in labs. That said there are two major issues now. Namely power source and Particle accelerators. (Mind you I have 0 particle accelerators and can produce and deposit 7.5b lp worth of power source per day so I’m not biased) the issue with PA is that it’s the second lowest LP per crew. This is way out of balance since the time it takes to mine and transport is astronomically more than any other component. It’s effectively worthless now. The second issue which is the largest issue is the Power source. It has the exact opposite problem as PA and what’s worse is that you can transport them to any base on the map seemlessly since they weigh only 2 and require very little transportation logistics to produce. To add to the problem all bases can accept PS so players like myself will be able to farm 7.5b lp per day for months until each base is filled with PS

author: [SAI] Sim [STAR]
content:
I know, guys, but this is not on our side. We can give feedback, but we cannot influence development in any way for two reasons: First, we don't have even 1% of the competence that the guys in SA have in any field: game design, graphic department, on-chain development, etc. Second, we can only give feedback on what we are currently seeing, which is something like 6 months old (SB core has been developed 6-ish months ago), if you ask me. It's like looking at the past to adjust the future, and it's wrong. As players, we can only wait for a more engaging module, but as the Star Atlas family, we can dream of how the whole ecosystem will be in the near future.

Personally, I don't like Elon Musk either; he's too fickle (I hope I used this term correctly XD). But if Michael is doing so, there must be a reason. It's called calculated risk.

This is just my idea, by the way, which could be the worst in the world hahaha.

content: guys, a speculation on Polis: from your point of view, will the jurisdictional and financial dominion of a territory exercised through polis by an individual or a guild be subordinated to the prior military occupation of the aforementioned territory or will it be independent? In short, if I have a polis, will I be able to impose myself on a territory with customs taxes and laws or will I have to first occupy it with the army, and then subsequently use polis to define laws and finance on that territory? Because in this case, if within the DAC there was only one polis owner with significant quantities of tokens, he could find himself in the absurd situation of being a problem for his own guild, as he would exercise power over his own companions, imposing himself on them.

content: TBH, we're still quite a ways out from fully fleshing that out internally. But think about how government and military work collectively in the real world. That could be paid to DACs and players, or potentially be used to pay for NPCs to patrol an area.

author: ROME|King Bryan-Titan Analytics [STAR]
content:
This whole DAC conversation turned funny.   It feels like anyone who doesn't understand how DAC ownership can be beneficial hasn't played any space MMO or any multiplayer game with territory rights.  You can't have a space MMO without group ownership.  I mean, you can, but it will be the jankiest thing ever created.   I think I saw a suggestion that individuals should hold power and not DACS.   Okay, welcome Virtu and Bodhi owning 2/3 of the map.  If ROME wanted territory they would need to appoint an individual to run it? Instead of ROME itself?   How do you share ownership/rights/permissions for using certain game assets?   How do people club together to oppose large individuals?   At this point, anyone opposed to DAC rights and ownership will eventually circle back when they are ready to hear it.  It is literally the life blood of any online game. Pretty shocked to hear resistance to it.

If the argument (Funcrackers) on the other hand is that we shouldn't build DAC mechanics into the game yet because the game is still being built, sure, I can understand that argument.
